_what_this_is: PRE-REGISTERED test of the operator's 2026-09-11 hypothesis: that the day is built from a few big directional legs, that the ORDER BOOK announces when one is about to start, and that the desk's existing drift detector can supply the direction. Written down BEFORE any P&L was computed on the combined rule, fixed for 60 forward sessions, and deliberately not tunable. The question it exists to answer is narrow and falsifiable: DOES BOOK THINNING ADD ANYTHING TO DRIFT ALONE?
registered_by: operator: 'yes build that test. pre register it'
hypothesis: Liquidity withdraws from the order book shortly before a directional leg begins. Thinning therefore signals WHEN a move is imminent; drift.compute() supplies WHICH WAY. The pair should beat drift alone.

_what_is_already_known_and_is_therefore_.what_was_measured_there: At the start of legs >= 40pt, 3-level book depth was 0.72x its matched-control level (54 vs 75, t=-12.45) and touch size 0.79x (11 vs 14, t=-7.79). Signed order-book imbalance at those moments was ~0.000 with only ~20% agreeing with the leg's direction - the book said a move was coming but NOT its direction.
_what_is_already_known_and_is_therefore_.why_this_disqualifies_the_window: The thinning effect was FOUND on that window, so a P&L computed there is a description of it, not a test of it. Those 21 sessions may be used only to verify the code runs and produces trades. Their P&L IS NOT EVIDENCE and must never be quoted as a result.
_what_is_already_known_and_is_therefore_.caveat_on_the_discovery_itself: The +/-2 minute measurement window straddles the pivot, so it cannot separate 'a thin book let price move' from 'the move consumed the book'. The forward test uses a STRICTLY CAUSAL trigger (below) which is immune to this, but the underlying mechanism remains unproven.

_why_one_lot: The IBKR paper engine fabricates a 0.1%-adverse fill on every lot beyond the first (91 of 91 deviations adverse, 62 lots carrying 66% of the desk's reported loss). At one lot the mechanism cannot engage, so every fill in this test is a real measurement. Size is NOT part of the hypothesis.

arms.A_drift_only: THE CONTROL, and the incumbent. Enter on drift.compute().confirmed, in drift's direction, first confirmation of the session.
arms.B_thinning_only: Enter on the thinning trigger alone, direction taken from drift's CURRENT direction field even if unconfirmed.
arms.C_both: THE HYPOTHESIS. Enter only when the thinning trigger fires AND drift is confirmed, in drift's direction.

_why_three_arms: The claim is not 'C makes money' - it is 'thinning ADDS to drift'. That is only answerable against A. If C and A are indistinguishable, the thinning trigger is decoration and the honest verdict is REFUTED even if both are positive.

trigger_thinning.definition: median(3-level total book size over the trailing 3 minutes) / median(3-level total book size over this session from 13:30Z up to 15 minutes ago)
trigger_thinning.causality: Both windows end strictly before the current minute. The baseline deliberately excludes the most recent 15 minutes so a slow bleed cannot drag its own baseline down with it.
trigger_thinning.hygiene: Minutes are dropped if the snapshot count is < 5, if ask1p <= bid1p (9% of snapshots are crossed or locked), or if ask1p takes only ONE distinct value in the minute - the last of these excludes the documented 19.6-hour frozen-ask window (200,708 consecutive snapshots) and any repeat of it.

trigger_direction.source: gazbot7.drift.compute() over minute bars from 13:30Z to the entry minute
trigger_direction.requires: r.confirmed is True and r.direction in ('UP','DOWN')
trigger_direction.causality: drift.read() is NOT used - it has no upper time bound and silently look-aheads when called retrospectively, returning a confident WRONG direction (measured on 2026-09-10: causal UP vs unbounded DOWN). Bars are sliced to the entry minute and passed to compute() directly.

entry: The OPEN of the next 1-minute bar after both conditions hold. Never a price inside the signal bar and never a level that has already passed - a fill that never printed is not a measurement.
exit: The desk's live rule: per-lot ladder at +50/+100/+200/+300 pt modelled as RESTING LIMIT orders, remainder flat at 20:40Z. No stop, matching the operator's standing instruction.
_secondary_diagnostic_only: A 150pt protective stop variant is recorded alongside but CANNOT change the verdict. It exists because the measured heat on a stopless hold is median 124pt and p90 346pt - $995 and $2,767 on 4 lots - and the operator should see what a stop would have cost or saved.
fees: MNQ $1.50 per round turn per contract.

verdict_rule.primary: C_both beats A_drift_only on mean P&L per trade, by a margin whose 95% bootstrap CI (day-clustered, 10000 resamples) excludes zero.
verdict_rule.supporting: C_both mean P&L per trade > 0 with t >= 2.0, net of fees.
verdict_rule.REFUTED: primary not met - i.e. thinning adds nothing detectable to drift.
verdict_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: fewer than 25 C-arm entries accumulated by session 60. This is the most likely outcome and must be reported as such rather than dressed up either way.

rules_of_engagement: DO NOT tune the 0.75 threshold. Not once. A moved threshold restarts the count at zero.
DO NOT add a third feature. Two is the entire design: one for WHEN, one for WHICH WAY.
DO NOT read the interim result as a verdict. n<60 sessions is not evidence here, by construction.
DO NOT drop it early because it looks bad. An unfavourable pre-registered result is the most valuable outcome this can produce.
DO NOT quote the 2026-08-14..09-11 discovery window as a result. It is where the effect was found.
RECORD every session whether anything fired or not - the sessions with no trigger are half the test.
If the depth capture is down for a session, mark it EXCLUDED with the reason. Do not silently skip it.
why_this_shape: The desk has one detector that works unattended (drift) and one filter that makes it testable (WATCH_RT), and neither is wired to anything. This test asks whether a THIRD, genuinely new signal - liquidity withdrawal - adds to the first. It is designed so the answer can be no. The discovery measurement was strong (t=-12.45) but it was measured around known pivots; the only thing that can promote it from an observation to an edge is a forward record against a control, fixed in advance.
status: ACTIVE - awaiting first eligible session 2026-09-12. Zero sessions counted.

_held_out_backtest_declared_before_runni.why_it_exists: Local depth.db starts 2026-08-14, which is the discovery window, so no out-of-sample depth appeared to exist. It does: B2 (b2raw:gazbotv7/plain/tape/book/MNQ/) archives the L2 book back to 2026-07-31. BACKBLAZE IS THE RECORD; the local disk is a CACHE.
_held_out_backtest_declared_before_runni.status_at_declaration: NEVER EXAMINED. No feature, threshold or arm has been computed on these days by anyone, at any point.
_held_out_backtest_declared_before_runni.rule_frozen: The registered rule is used EXACTLY as it stands: depth_ratio <= 0.75, drift.compute() confirmed, entry at the next bar's open, ladder as resting limits + 20:40Z flat, 1 lot, $1.50/RT. Nothing is tuned for this window. If it disappoints, that is the result.
_held_out_backtest_declared_before_runni.verdict_rule_for_this_window: Same as the forward test: C_both must beat A_drift_only. n=13 sessions cannot CONFIRM anything - it is far below the 25-entry floor - but it CAN refute, and a C arm that loses to its own control out-of-sample is a genuine negative result available today rather than in December.
_held_out_backtest_declared_before_runni.commitment: This is run ONCE. The threshold is not moved afterwards. If the result is poor the forward test still runs to 60 sessions, because a 13-day sample is not evidence enough to abandon a pre-registered design either.
